learn.title: A loop inside a loop
learn.body: You can put one loop inside another. The inner loop runs completely for every single pass of the outer loop. This is how programs work with grids, tables and patterns.

learn.title: A rectangle
learn.body: The outer loop makes rows. The inner loop prints one row.

learn.title: How many times
learn.body: The outer loop runs 3 times and the inner runs 4 times for each of them, so `printf("#")` runs 3 times 4, which is 12 times. After each row the outer loop prints a new line.

learn.title: A triangle
learn.body: The inner limit depends on the row, so each row is longer.

learn.title: Why a triangle appears
learn.body: Look at the inner loop `c < r`.

learn.title: do while
learn.body: A `do while` loop runs its block first and tests afterwards, so it always runs at least once. The start `n` is 10, the test `n < 5` is false from the start, yet the block still prints once. Note the semicolon after the closing parenthesis.

learn.title: Runs once
learn.body: A normal while loop would have run zero times here.
Use `for` when you know the count, `while` when you wait for a condition, and `do while` when you must run once first.

questions.prompt: An outer loop runs 3 times and an inner loop runs 4 times each. How many times does the inner block run in total? Type the number.
The rectangle program prints how many lines?
questions.explanation: Each outer pass prints one row followed by a new line, and there are 3 passes.

questions.prompt: In the triangle program, how many `#` are in the second row?
questions.explanation: In row 2 the inner loop runs while `c < 2`, so two times.

questions.prompt: The inner loop of a nested pair finishes \_\_ for each pass of the outer loop.
questions.explanation: Every outer pass restarts the inner loop and lets it run to the end.

choices: The block runs at least once
questions.explanation: The condition is tested after the block, not before.

questions.prompt: `int n = 10; do { n++; } while (n < 5);` What is `n` afterwards? Type the number.
questions.explanation: The block runs once, making `n` 11. The test is then false.

questions.prompt: A do while loop ends with a \_\_ after the condition.
Put the steps of printing the rectangle in order.
steps: Start the outer loop for a row
Run the inner loop to print the # symbols
questions.explanation: A row is finished before the next one begins.
